newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 23.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The Inkatha Freedom Party has demanded that the KwaZulu-Natal constitution, rejected by the Constitutional Court last year as an attempt to usurp central government powers, be adopted as a precondition for reconciliation with the African National Congress.

- The National Union of Mineworkers on Friday rejected a key element of a precedent-setting Chamber of Mines wage offer for this year which employers said was designed to deal with a "crisis of major proportions" in the gold mining industry.

- Yonbor Nominees, a group of minority shareholders in Sentrachem led by Capital Alliance directors Larry Nestadt and Gary Burg, have abandoned plans to go to court in a 600,000 rand damages suit against the chemical group.

- Changes to the Johannesburg Stock Exchange indices sparked fireworks on the exchange late on Friday, with some of the shares leaving the indices experiencing a dramatic fall in price while some of those which joined made spectacular gains.
- Standard Bank has adopted a bullish outlook on an interest-rate cut, announcing on Friday that it would drop home-loan interest rates on fixed and capped loans, ahead of the rest of the market.

- Gencor has played down reports of a shareholder revolt in Queensland Nickel Industries (QNI), the Australian hickel producer with which it announced last week it was merging its nickel interests in a A$2.3 billion deal.
- Motorists who use hand-held mobile phones face fines of up to 20,000 rand and a year's jail under legislation being drafted by the transport department.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Dealers' anger at the way in which brokerage firms sold or bought stock on Friday to change their portfolios to match the JSE's new indices might prompt the exchange to consider modifying its procedures for changing index compositions.
- Laid-off workers at New Age Beverages would not receive payouts from the Unemployment Insurance Fund, because the company had not paid employees' contributions into the fund, sources said.

- Gold prices ended on Friday below the important $340 an ounce level as both negative sentiment and concern in the platinum and palladium market knocked bullion, which fixed in the afternoon in London at $338.20.

- National Sorghum Breweries, which received a 70 million rand capital injection last November from India's United Breweries, would require an additional 50 million rand to put it on a sound financial footing, executive chairman Mohale Mahanyele said.
SAKE-BEELD

- Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals rejected criticism levelled at him and the bank by labour federation Cosatu, saying the central bank's comments on proposed changes to South Africa's labour were based on facts and were impartial.
- Citadel investment services said the rand was slightly undervalued against the dollar and sterling, but slightly overvalued against the mark and the yen.
- Brokers complained about possible manipulation of prices of certain shares during the change of the JSE's indices last Friday.
- The South African banking industry would shed about 10,000 jobs over the next three years, according to the financial sector's labour union, Sasbo.
THE STAR

- An amnesty hearing for the killers of Communist Party leader Chris Hani starts in Benoni east of Johannesburg on Monday amid the most stringent security measures yet seen at a Truth and Reconciliation Commission hearing.
- Education has been thrown into uncertainty by a court ruling which declared that Education Minister Sibusiso Bengu's efforts to redeploy teachers exceeded his authority.
